UPSTREAM: drivers/i2c/generic: Add config for marking device as probed Add a config option to the generic I2C device driver to indicate to the OS that this device should be probed before being added. This can be used to provide ACPI device instantiations to devices that may not actually exist on the board. For example, if multiple trackpad vendors are supported on the same board they can both be described in ACPI and the OS will probe the address and load the driver only if the device responds to the probe at that address. login: Explicitly remount the container with MS_RDONLY Turns out that even if the filesystem is mounted read-only outside the container, the same mount inside the container will preserve the flag that was passed explicitly (0, meaning read-write), even if the underlying filesystem was marked read-only. This change explicitly remounts the containers' rootfs with MS_RDONLY if the underlying filesystem is mounted read-only. CHROMIUM: tpm: Add driver for cr50 on I2C Add TPM 2.0 compatible I2C interface for chips with cr50 firmware. The firmware running on the currently supported H1 MCU requires a special driver to handle its specific protocol, and this makes it unsuitable to use tpm_tis_core_* and instead it must implement the underlying TPM protocol similar to the other I2C TPM drivers. - All 4 byes of status register must be read/written at once. - FIFO and burst count is limited to 63 and must be drained by AP. - Provides an interrupt to indicate when read response data is ready and when the TPM is finished processing write data. This driver is based on the existing infineon I2C TPM driver, which most closely matches the cr50 i2c protocol behavior. The driver is intentionally kept very similar in structure and style to the corresponding drivers in coreboot and depthcharge. syslinux: drop local copy We have a newer version in portage-stable now we want to use. Keep in mind that syslinux is not used on any official Chrome OS device as we have our own custom firmware everywhere. It is only used when booting Chromium OS. Our copy had a few custom changes: - Turn off the video cursor before booting the kernel - Sometimes disable display of the syslinux banner when booting - Disable display of all info messages The first patch is no longer needed: our boot splash code takes care of turning off the cursor before showing the screen, either directly (when USE=vtconsole), or by letting frecon do it when it creates the new VT. Disabling the boot banner happens only for some boot paths (e.g. the isolinux code), but not all (e.g. the serial port), and it disables only part of the banner. It also doesn't disable all messages that come up early on. In the end, it doesn't make things all the much more quiet to the point where we need to maintain it. The code also tried to disable the common writemsg function, but it is only called for info/debug messages, none of which are displayed by default. Which means it's kind of a pointless change. By dropping our custom syslinux version, we make the output a little bit more verbose for Chromium OS builds, but since we aren't silent now, it's not a big deal. BUG=chromium:508713 TEST=`emerge syslinux` uses the new one in portage-stable TEST=vmtests pass CQ-DEPEND=CL:382771 Change-Id: I922710079ac5f4c9ca9c177eab880a99ada1415e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/382772 Commit-Ready: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Richard Barnette <jrbarnette@google.com>
